# ADR 0061 — The cashier snapshot is a projection with one writer and a nightly comparison

- Status: **proposed** (spec:95 — this touches security and the data model)
- Date: 2026-09-05
- Slice: 6C

## Context

spec:1324 requires the till to evaluate a cashier's authority with no network, from the permission codes
and limits that travel with the catalogue. It also says, in the same sentence, that this is "a
**projection**, regenerated by the catalogue-revision trigger whenever a `role_assignment`,
`role_assignment_branch` or `role_permission` row affecting that principal changes (and on termination),
compared nightly against `actor_has()` like every other projection (D14), never edited by hand."

Two things follow that a plan must state or a later reader will get wrong.

## Decision

1. **One writer.** `app.refresh_pos_cashier(p_principal_id uuid)` is the only statement in the system that
   writes `pos_cashier.snapshot`. It is called by AFTER triggers on `role_assignment`,
   `role_assignment_branch`, `role_permission` and `branch_pos_policy`, and by 8C's termination trigger. No
   route, job or handler writes the column; Task 10 asserts that by scanning `apps/**` for the column name.
2. **Which codes it holds is DERIVED, never listed**: `select code from app.permission where module = 'pos'
   and code not like 'pos.sync.%'`, mirrored in TypeScript as `CASHIER_SNAPSHOT_CODES` over `PERMISSIONS`.
   A literal list would have to name 6D's codes before 6D seeds them. `pos.sync.*` is excluded because it
   is the *terminal's* authority (R8), never a cashier's.
3. **The server never reads it.** Sync apply re-verifies against `app.principal_has` and the
   `branch_pos_policy` row (spec:1324). The snapshot exists for the till and for nothing else.
4. **The nightly job reports and does not repair.** `pos.cashier.compare` recomputes every cashier's
   snapshot and writes one `app.audit_log` row with `table_name = 'cashier_snapshot_drift'` per differing
   cashier (§4.2.6's sentinel mechanism, third registered sentinel). Repairing would make a broken trigger
   invisible for exactly as long as the job kept running.

## Consequences

- A permission change is visible at the till only after the next catalogue pull. That is the design: the
  revision bumps in the same transaction as the grant, so the pull that follows carries it, and the *server*
  refuses anything the stale snapshot wrongly allowed.
- `refresh_pos_cashier` runs inside the writer's transaction. ~~It runs under the writer's RLS; a
  `branch_manager` cannot change a role assignment (they hold no `admin.role.assign`), so in practice the
  callers are the admin, `hr_payroll` and the system principal — all of which see every branch.~~ Corrected
  by the PR 12 review amendment below: those callers do **not** all see every branch or every company, so the
  refresh reads and writes as the tenant's system principal and restores the caller's actor before returning.
- Adding a POS permission code in a later slice changes no line here; the derivation picks it up, and T7's
  equality test between the SQL and TypeScript spellings is what keeps the two honest.

## Proposal preparation

Prepared for owner review on 2026-10-07 from [2026-09-05-dulja-phase-6c-staff-cashiers-branch-isolation.md](../superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-dulja-phase-6c-staff-cashiers-branch-isolation.md). The source proposal date above is preserved. This record is proposed; no owner acceptance or implementation is recorded here.

## What we are asking

Approve a trigger-maintained cashier snapshot for offline use, current server-side authority checks at sync apply, and nightly reporting of drift without automatic repair?

## PR 12 review amendment — the refresh runs as the tenant's system principal (2026-10-22, proposed)

The PR 12 review found that the Consequences bullet above ("all of which see every branch") did not hold.
Roles and their permissions belong to the whole tenant: `PUT /v1/admin/roles/{id}/permissions` is gated
`admin.role.manage` with `{ company: "any" }` (contracts §4.2.5's fourth variant), and creating a company
assigns no role in it. `pos_cashier` and `branch_pos_policy` carry Form A of `branch_isolation` (ADR 0062),
which admits only a principal with a live role assignment in that company and branch. So an administrator
whose assignments are all in company X, or one restricted to branch B1, could edit a role that company Y's or
branch B2's cashiers hold; the trigger called `refresh_pos_cashier` for those cashiers, the function selected
the row under the writer's RLS, found nothing and returned. Their snapshots kept the codes the edit had just
changed: a removed code was still authorised offline and refused at sync (the ticket lands in
needs-attention), an added one was refused at the till, and the nightly comparison reported the drift every
night without repairing it (decision 4).

Decision (owner direction 2026-10-22: best practice), implemented in migration 0067 section 3:

1. `app.refresh_pos_cashier` looks up the tenant's system principal and sets `app.actor_id` to it,
   transaction-locally, for its select and its update; it then restores the caller's value. The system
   principal passes every `branch_isolation` form, as it does for the nightly job (R8, spec:2179). A tenant
   with no system principal is refused `ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING`; bootstrap creates one for every tenant.
2. This grants nothing. Which codes and limits the snapshot holds is derived only from `app.principal_has` and
   the branch's `branch_pos_policy` row, so full visibility only lets the projection be computed correctly.
   `pos_cashier` has no audit trigger and no actor stamp (0065), so the system actor appears in no record; the
   writer's own rows — the `role_permission` or `role_assignment` change and its audit row — keep the
   writer's actor, including later rows of the same multi-row statement and later statements of the same
   transaction.
3. RLS stays forced. No `SECURITY DEFINER`, no `BYPASSRLS`, no permissive policy and no change to the frozen
   `{ company: "any" }` gate.
4. The restore needs no exception block. A caller can observe an error raised inside the function only from
   an enclosing savepoint or exception block or after its transaction aborts, and PostgreSQL reverts a
   transaction-local `set_config` made inside an aborted (sub)transaction. The function therefore has a
   single exit with the restore on it. An exception block would cost a subtransaction per call, and
   `refresh_pos_cashier_for_role` makes one call per principal holding the edited role.
5. Every path is fixed at once, because all four triggers, `createCashier` / `revokeCashier` and 8C's planned
   termination trigger go through this one function. No trigger is renamed, so `catalogue_revision` still
   fires before `snapshot_revision_stamp`.

`packages/db/test/staff/cashier-snapshot.test.ts` proves it: a `role_permission` edit by an administrator of
company X alone refreshes company Y's cashier, and an edit by one restricted to branch B1 refreshes a cashier
at B2. In both cases the codes and revision change, `findSnapshotDrift` finds nothing, and the writer's actor
holds afterwards and on the audit rows. Both cases fail on the tree before this amendment.
